summary: Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested as a research fellow at Humboldt University and a part-time teacher at Heidelberg University.

Monica Esposito (1962–2011) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (1981–1987) and Paris Diderot University (PhD, ~1988–1993), later serving as an associate professor at Kyoto University from around 2003 to 2011.

Monier Monier-Williams (1819–1899) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson, later teaching at East India Company College (~1844–1858) and Cheltenham College (~1858–1860) before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit from 1860.

Monika Horstmann is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Bonn (~1963–1970), Australian National University (~1978–1980), University of Cologne (~1982–1992), and Heidelberg University, where she was attested as emeritus professor in 2009.

Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University and LMU Munich, served as a professor at LMU Munich (~1994–2016) and Free University of Berlin (~2014–2016), and joined the Saxon Academy of Sciences in 2016.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Rissho University (attested 1984), Sendai College (~1987–2003), and Hosen Gakuen College (~2004).

Moritz Abraham Stern (1807–1894) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss, subsequently holding an academic post at the University of Göttingen from 1830 to 1884.

Moriz Haupt (1808–1874) was a scholar of linguistics who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig University (~1826–1831). He later held academic appointments at Leipzig University (~1837–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1874).

Moriz Winternitz (1863–1937) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He was a professor at the German University in Prague (~1899–1934) and a visiting professor at Visva-Bharati University (1922–1923).

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching posts at Yale, UCLA, Victoria University of Wellington, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler (1890–1976) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London. He served at Amgueddfa Cymru (1920–1926), the London Museum (1926–1944), UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1937–1944), and as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1952).

Morton Klass (1927–2001) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, later holding posts at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).
Mother Sayamagyi (1925–2017) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She was a disciple of Sayagyi U Ba Khin and eventually succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi (1945–2015) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~1968–1974) studying under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. In 1975, he became a professor at Shuchiin University.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima and completed degrees at the University of Tsukuba and the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Tsukuba in ~1994.

Motoichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1978 and later served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University from around 1986 to 1993.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested between 1970 and 1990) and held appointments in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982 and 1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (ended 1999). He later held posts at Leipzig University (attested 2005) and Heidelberg University (attested 2007–2009).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Indology. He has served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums of Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).
Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University and later served as the university's president from around 1949 to 1978.
